subject: Authority switch + TLS proxy playbook for private endpoint cutover
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Carter <alice.carter@acme-payments.com>, Tom Brennan <tom.brennan@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Authority switch + TLS proxy playbook for private endpoint cutover

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Per our call, attached is a concise playbook for transferring DNS authority and performing TLS termination at Acme's edge proxy during the private deployment cutover. The goal is to minimize blast radius while meeting your compliance requirements (no customer keys leave your HSM, audit trail for cert handoff).

High-level proposed window (example):
- Prep (T-72h): DNS zone export + TTL reductions to 60s, dry-run cert issuance in staging CA.
- Cutover (T0): Switch authoritative NS to Acme-managed zone, update edge-proxy listener cert to Redwood-provided cert bundle (or mutual TLS if required).
- Canary (T0+30m): 5% traffic routed to new path, verify tracing + auth.
- Roll forward (T0+2h): Expand routing to 100% if no errors; otherwise rollback to previous NS and cert.

Key decisions we need from Acme before T-72h:
1) Will Acme host the authoritative name servers (yes/no)?
2) Do you require mutual TLS to Redwood backends, or TLS termination at the proxy only?
3) HSM/KMS policy for private key custody (customer-kept vs Redwood-managed temporary key escrow).

Attachments: redwood-tls-proxy-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook), dns-zone-export-acme.txt (sample zone), cert-rotation-schedule.csv (rotation cadence).

Next steps: please confirm answers to the three items above and propose a 2-hour maintenance window (weekday preferred) next week.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Strategic Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Carter <alice.carter@acme-payments.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brennan <tom.brennan@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Authority switch + TLS proxy playbook for private endpoint cutover

Sergio —

Appreciate the playbook. A couple quick clarifications from security before we lock the window:
- We will host authoritative NS during the cutover (Acme-managed).
- We require mutual TLS to Redwood for any customer-identifiable traffic; termination at our proxy only is allowed for non-sensitive control plane calls.
- All private keys for customer-facing endpoints must remain inside our HSM (no export). Temporary certs for canary are ok if private key material never leaves HSM (ACME with ACME-AUTHZ using our CA is preferred).

Also need confirmation of audit logging for cert installs and an endpoint where we can pull traces during the canary. Can you include a sample audit record format?

Regards,
Alice Carter
Director, InfoSec — Acme Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Carter <alice.carter@acme-payments.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Authority switch + TLS proxy playbook for private endpoint cutover

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick answers. Below are concrete mappings and the audit example you requested. I've kept the steps as discrete runbook items we can walk through in the maintenance window.

Runbook highlights (technical):
1) DNS prep
   - Export Redwood zone file (attached dns-zone-export-acme.txt) and reduce TTLs to 60s for cutover-relevant records (A, CNAME, SRV).
   - Provide glue records and validation tokens to Acme for NS change.
2) Cert issuance
   - Option A (preferred for key custody): ACME protocol integrated with Acme's internal CA. Redwood will request an ACME cert; Acme's ACME server performs AuthZ and signs; private key never leaves HSM.
   - Option B (customer provides cert bundle): Acme generates keys in HSM and uploads CSR; we install certs on the proxy via out-of-band signed attestation.
3) Proxy config and TLS termination
   - Edge proxy (Envoy) will be configured with SNI routing to the private runtime. For mutual TLS to Redwood backends, enable client auth on the proxy-to-backend listener; Redwood will present an mTLS client cert issued by Acme (short-lived).
   - If termination occurs at Acme proxy only, Redwood will accept connections from Acme proxy's IP ranges and enforce mTLS.
4) Observability and audit
   - Audit record sample (JSON lines): {"timestamp":"2027-04-19T16:00:00Z","action":"cert_installed","subject":"service-acme.private.redwood","actor":"deploy-bot","method":"acme","note":"key-kept-in-hsm","trace_id":"trace-abc123"}
   - Redwood will push canary traces to the Acme short-lived pre-signed S3/HTTPS endpoint and expose per-route tokenized trace links during T0+30m.
5) Rollback
   - Keep previous cert + NS records cached; if any 5xx spike or mutual TLS failures >1% of flows for 15m, revert NS and proxy config.

Security controls: no private key export, all cert install actions require a 2-person approval in case of manual CSR installs. We will create an auditable log entry per install and provide the log extract.

Attachments referenced above include the playbook PDF with step-by-step commands and a cert rotation CSV with suggested TTLs/rotation windows.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Authority switch + TLS proxy playbook for private endpoint cutover

Quick additions from infra/SRE perspective:
- Routing: we'll add a traffic-split rule so we can send 5% to the new path using header-based canary (X-Canary-Acme) to avoid DNS propagation variance in the first 30m.
- Metrics: need Acme to provision a temporary scrape target for our Prometheus pushgateway or provide a short-lived push token so we can surface backend errors in the same dashboard.
- Egress: confirm outbound IP ranges for Acme proxy to whitelist to avoid unexpected blocked egress during canary.

I'll update the runbook with Envoy examples and the exact traceroute/troubleshoot commands. Link to the draft runbook: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/private-cutover (internal).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Authority switch + TLS proxy playbook for private endpoint cutover

Thanks everyone — this looks good.

Decision summary:
- Acme will host authoritative NS.
- ACME integration with Acme's CA (Option A) is preferred; private keys remain in HSM.
- Mutual TLS required for customer-identifiable traffic; Redwood to provide short-lived client certs issued by Acme for backend auth.

Action owners & timeline:
- Acme security (Alice): provide ACME endpoint + HSM CSR flow by EOD Thu (2027-04-22).
- Redwood infra (Marissa/Karthik): prepare runbook and staging test by Fri (2027-04-23).
- Sales/PM (Sergio): coordinate maintenance window and stakeholder comms for the week of 2027-04-26.

I'll draft a one-page change notice for legal/ops and share for sign-off. Once Alice confirms the ACME endpoint and token, we can schedule the cutover.

Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference
